"'''Baby Baby'''" is a pop song by American recording artist [[Amy Grant]] and it was issued as the first single from her eighth studio album, ''[[Heart in Motion]]'' (1991). The song was written by Grant and [[Keith Thomas (producer)|Keith Thomas]], who also produced it. It was released on January 18, 1991, through [[A&M Records]] and topped the US [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] chart for two consecutive weeks in April 1991, becoming the first in a string of hits from ''Heart in Motion''. At the [[34th Annual Grammy Awards]] in 1992, the song received three Grammy Award nominations, including [[Grammy Award for Song of the Year|Song of the Year]] and [[Grammy Award for Record of the Year|Record of the Year]]. Its music video was directed by D.J. Webster and first aired in March 1991.

"Baby Baby" is a pop song by American recording artist Amy Grant and it was issued as the first single from her eighth studio album, Heart in Motion (1991). The song was written by Grant and Keith Thomas, who also produced it. It was released on January 18, 1991, through A&M Records and topped the US Billboard Hot 100 chart for two consecutive weeks in April 1991, becoming the first in a string of hits from Heart in Motion. At the 34th Annual Grammy Awards in 1992, the song received three Grammy Award nominations, including Song of the Year and Record of the Year. Its music video was directed by D.J. Webster and first aired in March 1991.

sections.heading: Background
sections.wikitext: The music was written by [[Keith Thomas (producer)|Keith Thomas]]. Grant had foreseen the song's success, and requested that Thomas write the song.<ref name="mount"/> He complied under the only condition that the song would be titled "Baby Baby". Grant experienced difficulty in writing the lyrics; she attempted to write a romantic-sounding song but could not prevent it from sounding like "some overgrown football jock with no vocabulary trying desperately to be romantic".<ref name="billboardbook"/> Later, she came to inspiration upon having seen her six-week-old daughter Millie. In the ''[[Heart in Motion]]'' booklet are the words: ''This song is dedicated to Millie, whose six-week-old face was my inspiration''. Millie would also appear on stage during Grant's performance at the [[34th Grammy Awards]].

sections.heading: Composition
sections.wikitext:
{{Listen
| filename=Amy Grant - Baby Baby.ogg
| title="Baby Baby"
| description=The first 32 seconds of Amy Grant's "Baby Baby"
| format=[[Ogg]]
}}
The song is almost four minutes in length and is composed in the [[Key (music)|key]] of [[F-sharp major]], set in the [[time signature]] of {{music|time|4|4}} [[common time]] with a moderate [[tempo]] of 98 beats per minute. In the middle of the song, the key is [[Modulation (music)|changed]] to [[A-flat major]], then for a short amount of time goes back to F{{sharp}} major and finally ends with A{{flat}} major. Grant's vocal range spans from F<sub>3</sub> to D♯<sub>5</sub>.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.musicnotes.com/sheetmusic/mtd.asp?ppn=MN0052923|title=Baby Baby|last1=Amy|first1=Grant|last2=Keith|first2=Thomas|date=July 24, 2006|website=Musicnotes.com|access-date=April 1, 2020|last3=Amy|first3=Grant|last4=Tori|first4=Kelly}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://tunebat.com/Info/Baby-Baby-Amy-Grant/42T9a9H2rm7kKRULZI6222|title=Key & BPM for Baby, Baby by Amy Grant {{!}} Tunebat|website=tunebat.com|access-date=April 1, 2020}}</ref>

The song consists of three verses that are interrupted by a [[Bridge (music)|bridge]], "'Stop for a minute, baby I'm so glad you're mine". Lyrically, the song praises that special someone and expresses love that started since the day her heart was "put in motion". The [[Refrain|chorus]] is the source of the album's title: "And ever since the day you put my heart in motion, baby I realized that there's just no gettin' over you". It [[Fade (audio engineering)|fades out]] with the lyrics:
{{poemquote|1=
Don't stop givin' love
Don't stop, no
(Baby I'm so glad)
Glad that you're mine
Baby I'm glad
}}

sections.heading: Critical reception
sections.wikitext: Pan-European magazine ''[[Music & Media]]'' wrote that Grant "still sounds grand on this danceable pop tune."<ref>{{cite magazine|title=New Releases: Singles|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1991/MM-1991-04-13.pdf|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=8|issue=15|date=April 13, 1991|page=12|accessdate=December 11, 2022}}</ref> In their review of the ''Heart in Motion'' album, ''Music & Media'' complimented "Baby Baby" as "heavenly".<ref>{{cite magazine|title=New Releases: Albums|url=https://worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-and-Media/90s/1991/MM-1991-04-27.pdf|magazine=[[Music & Media]]|volume=8|issue=17|date=April 27, 1991|page=12|accessdate=December 11, 2022}}</ref> [[James Hamilton (DJ and journalist)|James Hamilton]] from ''[[Record Mirror]]'' commented, "With a coincidentally apt catalogue number, the white [[Gospel music|gospel]] superstar's US chart topping secular smash is a catchy pop song on radio but becomes a hard "choon" on 12-inch in its chunkily chugged jiggly jogging 98–0bpm Heart In Motion Mix, with a poppier rolling No Getting Over You Mix too."<ref>{{cite magazine|first=James|last=Hamilton|url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/UK/Music-Week/1991/MW-1991-05-25.pdf#page=22|title=DJ Directory: Hot Vinyl|magazine=[[Music Week]], in [[Record Mirror]] (Dance Update Supplemental Insert)|date=May 25, 1991|page=6|access-date=September 12, 2025|author-link=James Hamilton (DJ and journalist)}}</ref>
sections.text: Pan-European magazine Music & Media wrote that Grant "still sounds grand on this danceable pop tune." In their review of the Heart in Motion album, Music & Media complimented "Baby Baby" as "heavenly". James Hamilton from Record Mirror commented, "With a coincidentally apt catalogue number, the white gospel superstar's US chart topping secular smash is a catchy pop song on radio but becomes a hard "choon" on 12-inch in its chunkily chugged jiggly jogging 98–0bpm Heart In Motion Mix, with a poppier rolling No Getting Over You Mix too."

sections.heading: Chart performance
sections.wikitext: "Baby Baby" was Amy Grant's biggest hit since her 1986 duet with [[Peter Cetera]], "[[The Next Time I Fall]]". In the United States, "Baby Baby" became Grant's second number-one hit on the pop charts and her first as a solo artist, topping the [[Billboard Hot 100|''Billboard'' Hot 100]] (replacing [[Wilson Phillips]]' "[[You're in Love (Wilson Phillips song)|You're in Love]]" from the top spot) and [[Hot Adult Contemporary Tracks|Adult Contemporary]] charts for two and three weeks, respectively. It also made Grant the first [[Christian pop]] singer to have a number-one single in the United States.<ref name="vindicator"/> The single reached the Top Ten in ten countries, in addition to reaching No. 11 in Switzerland. In the United Kingdom, "Baby Baby" was the singer's first (and only) Top Five hit in that country, reaching No. 2 in the [[UK Singles Chart]]. "Baby Baby" went on to become Grant's biggest hit single and one of the most successful singles of 1991.

sections.heading: Development and release
sections.wikitext:
[[File:AmyGrantBabyVideo.PNG|thumb|left|Grant singing and dancing along with her on-screen love interest, played by Jme Stein.<ref>{{cite magazine|url=https://www.rollingstone.com/music/music-country/amy-grant-tori-kelly-give-baby-baby-a-makeover-the-ram-report-73883/|title=Amy Grant, Tori Kelly Give "Baby Baby" a Makeover: The Ram Report|magazine=[[Rolling Stone]]|date=April 29, 2016|access-date=May 10, 2019}}</ref>]]
The accompanying music video for "Baby Baby" was directed by D.J. Webster.<ref name="spokesman"/> and edited by Scott C. Wilson. According to Webster, the video's main idea was to create a picture of the relationship that everybody wants.<ref name="spokesman"/> Grant added, "I think when you get film where there is a good sense of humor and mutual respect and people are just having a good time, everybody wants a piece of that".<ref name="spokesman"/> Its beginning features Grant receiving attention from other men, and her staying loyal to her lover, portrayed by model Jme Stein (who also appeared in her other video from that album "[[Good for Me (song)|Good for Me]]"). At some point Stein is seen singing along with Grant and at the end lip-syncing to the words "Baby I'm so glad". The rest of the video features the couple having fun together.

thumb|left|Grant singing and dancing along with her on-screen love interest, played by Jme Stein.
The accompanying music video for "Baby Baby" was directed by D.J. Webster. and edited by Scott C. Wilson. According to Webster, the video's main idea was to create a picture of the relationship that everybody wants. Grant added, "I think when you get film where there is a good sense of humor and mutual respect and people are just having a good time, everybody wants a piece of that". Its beginning features Grant receiving attention from other men, and her staying loyal to her lover, portrayed by model Jme Stein (who also appeared in her other video from that album "Good for Me"). At some point Stein is seen singing along with Grant and at the end lip-syncing to the words "Baby I'm so glad". The rest of the video features the couple having fun together.

sections.heading: Release and reception
sections.wikitext:
The video first aired in March 1991, although [[MTV]] didn't air it until it had become too popular not to.<ref name="bostonglobe"/> A music critic [[J.D. Considine]] praised the video, writing that "the ''Baby Baby'' clip defines the way most of us imagine her. It was hardly typical video fare, with no special effects or distant locales; all it offered was Grant and a good-looking guy cavorting and acting pretty as she lip-synced to the song. Yet there was something genuinely appealing about the image it conveyed, something that made viewers want to see the thing again".<ref name="spokesman"/> It received a nomination for [[MTV Video Music Award for Best Female Video|Best Female Video]] at the [[1991 MTV Video Music Awards]], but lost to [[Janet Jackson]]'s "[[Love Will Never Do (Without You)|Love Will Never Do]]".{{cn|date=May 2025}}

It's available on the 1992 music video tape ''The Heart in Motion Video Collection'' and 2004 music video [[DVD]] ''Greatest Videos 1986–2004''. A live performance is available on the 2006 DVD ''Time Again… Amy Grant Live''.
